problems.title: A quadratic inequality in cosine
problems.question: Solve 2cos²x+5cosx+2≥0.
steps: Since t+2 is positive on [-1,1], the inequality is t≥-1/2.
Thus x lies from -2π/3 to 2π/3 in each period.

problems.title: Convert cosine to sine
problems.question: Solve cosx=sin5x.
steps: 5x=π/2-x+2πk gives x=π/12+kπ/3.
5x=π/2+x+2πk gives x=π/8+kπ/2.

problems.title: Simplification with domain and range
problems.question: Find the domain and range of f(x)=cosx/(1+sinx)+(1+sinx)/cosx.
problems.idea: Combine the fractions before reading the range.
steps: The original denominators require cosx≠0; this also excludes sinx=-1.
On that domain cosx takes every value in [-1,0)∪(0,1].
Its reciprocal doubled therefore takes every value ≤-2 or ≥2.

problems.title: A negative cotangent reverses the inequality
problems.question: Solve |x-sin9|cot9>cos9, with 9 in radians.
steps: Divide by cot9, reversing the inequality: |x-sin9|<cos9/cot9=sin9.
Since sin9>0, the resulting open interval is sin9-sin9<x<sin9+sin9.

problems.title: Absolute tangent equals tangent squared
problems.question: Solve |cot(2x-π/2)|=1/cos²2x-1.
steps: Put v=|tan2x|≥0. Then v=v², so v=0 or 1.
Thus tan2x=0,1 or -1.
All three branches satisfy the original domain.
problems.answer: x=kπ/2 or x=π/8+kπ/2 or x=-π/8+kπ/2, k∈ℤ.

problems.title: Use sum and difference angles in a system
problems.question: Solve tanx+tany=2, cosxcosy=1/2.
problems.idea: Multiply the tangent equation by cosxcosy.
steps: The first equation gives x+y=π/2+2πk.
Hence cos(x+y)=0, and the second identity gives cos(x-y)=1, so x-y=2πm.
Adding and subtracting determines x,y.

problems.title: A pyramid with equal edge inclinations
problems.question: A pyramid has an isosceles right base of hypotenuse 5 cm. Every lateral edge makes angle α with the base. Find its total surface area.
problems.idea: The apex projects to the base circumcenter, the hypotenuse midpoint.
formulas: Base area=25/4; circumradius R=5/2; height h=Rtanα.
steps: The two equal base legs have length 5/√2. Their distance from the circumcenter is 5/(2√2).
The face on the hypotenuse has area 5h/2=25tanα/4.
Each other face has slant height √(h²+25/8) and area 25√(1+2tan²α)/8.
Add the base and all three faces.

problems.title: Equal dihedral angles determine an inradius
problems.question: A pyramid of height h has an isosceles trapezoid base with acute angle α. Every lateral face makes angle β with the base. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: The projected apex is equally far from all base sides.
formulas: Base inradius r=h cotβ; face slant height l=h/sinβ; lateral area=Pl/2.
steps: The tangential trapezoid has height 2r, so each leg is 2r/sinα.
Its bases sum to its legs, hence perimeter P=8r/sinα.
Therefore lateral area=4rh/(sinαsinβ).
Substitute r=hcosβ/sinβ.

problems.title: An oblique triangular prism
problems.question: All edges of a triangular prism are 12 cm. One upper vertex projects to the lower base’s centroid. Find total surface area.
problems.idea: The bases are equilateral, but the lateral edges are oblique.
formulas: A face on vectors u,v has area √(|u|²|v|²-(u·v)²).
steps: Take A=(0,0,0),B=(12,0,0),C=(6,6√3,0). The displacement to A₁ is v=(6,2√3,4√6), since |v|=12.
For faces on AB and AC, u·v=72, giving area √(144²-72²)=72√3 each.
For face BC, u·v=0, giving area 144.
The two base areas total 72√3. Sum all five faces: 144+216√3.

problems.title: A line clipped by the base and top
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has every edge a. K is on the centroid axis with OK=3O₁K. Find the length inside the prism of the line through K parallel to CA₁.
problems.idea: Parameterize by the horizontal side vector A-C.
formulas: K has height 3a/4; line direction v=(A-C,a), |v|=a√2.
steps: Write the line as K+tv. Its horizontal projection through the centroid meets the triangular base boundary at t=-1/3 and t=1/3.
The vertical bounds 0≤3a/4+ta≤a give -3/4≤t≤1/4.
Both conditions hold for -1/3≤t≤1/4, an interval of length 7/12.
Multiply by |v|.
